title: Sum of Powers: Extension to Non-Integer Exponents
description: Extends Faulhaber's formulas to real exponents via the p-series ζ(s) = ∑ 1/n^s. Proves convergence dichotomy (iff s > 1), recovers ζ(2) = π²/6 and ζ(4) = π⁴/90, establishes term and zeta monotonicity, and bridges real-exponent theory to integer power sums.

sections.title: Module Setup and Imports
sections.summary: Imports ZetaValues, PSeries, InfiniteSum, and Pow.Real. Sets maxHeartbeats for heavy elaboration.

sections.title: Part I: Convergence Dichotomy
sections.summary: Proves ∑ (n^s)⁻¹ converges iff s > 1 via Cauchy condensation (internally in Mathlib).

sections.title: Part II: Known Values
sections.summary: Recovers ζ(2) = π²/6 and ζ(4) = π⁴/90 in tsum form from Mathlib.

sections.title: Part III: Term Monotonicity
sections.summary: Proves (n^s)⁻¹ is antitone in s for n ≥ 1 (weak) and strictly for n ≥ 2.

sections.title: Part IV: Zeta Monotonicity
sections.summary: States ζ(s) is antitone. Sorry: tsum ordering not yet assembled.

sections.title: Parts V-VI: Bounds
sections.summary: States ζ(s) ≥ 1 and ζ(s) ≤ π²/6 for s ≥ 2. Both sorry.

sections.title: Part VII: Partial Sums
sections.summary: Defines partialZeta, proves convergence and monotonicity in number of terms.

sections.title: Part VIII: Bridge to Integer Exponents
sections.summary: Connects rpow to nat pow via rpow_natCast. Proves summability and convergence for integer k.

sections.title: Verification
sections.summary: Type-checks all 14 results. 11 proved, 3 with sorry.

overview.historicalContext: Faulhaber (1631) published formulas for ∑k^m for integer m up to m = 17. Euler (1734) made the revolutionary leap to non-integer exponents by computing ∑1/n² = π²/6 (the Basel problem), launching analytic number theory. The convergence dichotomy at s = 1 — where the harmonic series diverges (Oresme, c. 1360) but ∑1/n^{1+ε} converges for any ε > 0 — is connected to the prime number theorem via the Euler product ∏(1 - p^{-s})^{-1} = ζ(s). Riemann's 1859 memoir extended the domain to ℂ, revealing the connection between prime distribution and the zeros of ζ(s).
overview.problemStatement: Extend Faulhaber's integer power sums to real exponents $s \in \mathbb{R}$ by studying $\zeta(s) = \sum 1/n^s$: prove convergence dichotomy, recover known values, establish monotonicity and bounds, and bridge back to integer exponents.
overview.proofStrategy: Eight parts following the logical dependency chain. Part I wraps Mathlib's convergence criterion. Part II recovers zeta values. Part III proves term-wise antitonicity via rpow monotonicity and inversion. Parts IV-VI state zeta-level properties (sorry: tsum comparison). Part VII provides constructive partial sums. Part VIII bridges to integer exponents via rpow_natCast.
keyInsights: The p-series convergence threshold at s = 1 separates integrable from non-integrable power-law decay via the Cauchy condensation test
Euler's Basel problem ζ(2) = π²/6 reveals a deep connection between discrete arithmetic and continuous geometry
The general formula ζ(2k) = (-1)^{k+1} B_{2k}(2π)^{2k}/(2(2k)!) gives all even zeta values, while no closed form is known for odd values
The bridge theorem rpow_inv_eq_nat_inv via rpow_natCast connects real-exponent analysis to integer-exponent combinatorics
The 3 remaining sorries are routine tsum ordering comparisons suitable for automated proof search
prerequisites: Real-valued power series and summability (tsum, Summable)
Zeta values and Bernoulli numbers from Mathlib
Real rpow (generalized exponentiation via exp and log)

conclusion.summary: 11 of 14 results fully proved including convergence dichotomy, Basel problem recovery, term monotonicity, partial sum convergence, and the rpow-to-natpow bridge. 3 sorries remain in tsum ordering comparisons.
conclusion.implications: The bridge from Faulhaber to ζ(s) is the first step toward formalizing special values of L-functions. The 3 remaining sorries are routine and likely Aristotle-provable.
openQuestions: Close the 3 tsum ordering sorries using Mathlib's tsum_le_tsum and le_tsum
